subject.title: [Feature]: Capability-based permissions for skills/tools (default-deny high-risk actions)

question: What public capability taxonomy, grant storage model, default-deny rollout, and enforcement boundary should OpenClaw adopt for skills/tools?
rationale: The issue defines public plugin/skill metadata, persisted authorization state, security semantics, audit behavior, and upgrade compatibility that cannot be safely inferred from existing name-based policy and hook-time approval surfaces.

options.title: Approve Phased Core Capability Model
options.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics and design grant, filtering, execution-check, and audit layers behind a maintainer-approved contract before default-deny enforcement ships.

options.title: Limit To Advisory Descriptors First
options.body: Add visible capability declarations for inspection and policy plugins while deferring grants and enforcement to later RFCs.

options.title: Keep Governance Plugin-Only
options.body: Close or narrow the core item if maintainers decide current hooks, optional tools, and external governance plugins are the intended boundary for this policy class.

recommendation.title: Approve Phased Core Capability Model
recommendation.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics and design grant, filtering, execution-check, and audit layers behind a maintainer-approved contract before default-deny enforcement ships.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is already active in the issue's security/product review and has the strongest adjacent routing evidence across approvals, gateway, and plugin surfaces.
